summary: Two of the five modules are directly relevant to a chat UI; none contains a full transcript renderer. discussions.rs (src-tauri/src/discussions.rs) IS already a Codex session JSONL parser, but only at the summary level: it scans CODEX_HOME/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-<ts>-<uuid>.jsonl files per account, parses line 0 (session_meta) fully, then uses a cheap `line.contains("\"type\":\"user_message\"")` filter to count messages, extract a title/preview from the first real user message, and read cumulative token_count. It also builds a flat prompt-history index of ALL real user messages (text truncated to 600 chars), filtering synthetic `<environment_context>`/`<user_instructions>` messages. Crucially, agent_message lines are only COUNTED, never extracted — there is no transcript extractor and no tool-call/function-call parsing. However, all the plumbing needed to write one exists: rollout discovery (collect_rollouts in account_usage.rs), filename/uuid/timestamp parsing, session_id-vs-rollout_id fork semantics (Codex writes a NEW file per resume sharing payload.session_id; collapse_forks picks the newest file as HEAD with the fullest history), and copy/delete/claim commands. agent_room.rs is a separate, already-working chat system: an in-process axum MCP server (POST /mcp, bearer-token per PTY via CST_ROOM_TOKEN) where Codex agents exchange Room/Dm/System messages (RoomMessage {id, ts, from, fromLabel, to, kind, text}), persisted to agent-room/messages.jsonl, with an "operator" ident the human UI posts as (room_send) and reads via polling (room_messages). The frontend (src/main.ts) already renders this room as a message list with an input — a mini chat UI pattern to copy. account_usage.rs parses the same rollouts for cumulative token_count and turn_context model (useful for per-session cost badges in chat). metrics.rs is pool/global usage bookkeeping plus cost_for_usage pricing. kombai.rs is unrelated (embedded code-server in an iframe). Bottom line: the JSONL event vocabulary (session_meta, user_message, agent_message, token_count, turn_context, event_msg) is already known and partially parsed; a chat UI needs one new backend command (get_discussion_transcript) reusing these helpers, plus a live-update strategy (JSONL tail or Codex structured output), since live sessions currently stream raw PTY bytes to xterm.js.
keyFacts: YES, a Codex session JSONL parser already exists (discussions.rs) — but it extracts only summaries (title/preview/counts/tokens), NOT full transcripts; agent_message content is counted via string-contains but never deserialized or returned.

Rollout file format is fully mapped in code comments: line 0 = session_meta (payload.session_id, payload.id, cwd, timestamp, cli_version, large base_instructions); following lines = user_message, agent_message, token_count (cumulative under payload.info.total_token_usage), turn_context (payload.model), wrapped as {timestamp, type, payload}. Path: CODEX_HOME/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-<localTs>-<uuid>.jsonl.

Fork semantics are critical for transcripts: every `codex resume` writes a NEW rollout file (new filename uuid + payload.id) but keeps payload.session_id; collapse_forks() groups them and the HEAD (newest started_at) file contains the most complete history (message_count = max across forks). A transcript view should read the HEAD file only.

Synthetic user messages must be filtered in a chat UI: is_synthetic_prompt() skips messages starting with '<environment_context>' or '<user_instructions>' (NOT a blanket '<' prefix — real prompts can start with '<').

list_prompt_history already returns per-message structured data (PromptEntry: sessionId, accountId, filePath, cwd, per-message RFC3339 timestamp, sessionTitle, text truncated to 600 chars) — the closest existing thing to a message-level API, but user messages only.

agent_room.rs is ALREADY a chat system with a message model directly reusable for UI: RoomMessage {id:u64, ts, from, fromLabel, to:Option, kind: room|dm|system, text (max 8000 chars, control-chars stripped)}; persisted JSONL log, monotonic ids usable as cursors, tokio broadcast channel for long-poll (wait_for_messages, max 55s), operator ident 'operator' for the human.

Frontend already polls room_messages and renders roomMessages: RoomMessage[] with a send box (sendRoomMessage -> invoke('room_send', {text, to})) — an existing in-app chat rendering pattern in src/main.ts (~lines 1254-1400).

All discussion parsing is on-demand full rescans (spawn_blocking + one thread per account, re-reading every rollout file each call) — fine for a list view, but a live chat view needs incremental tailing, which does not exist yet.
Performance pattern used everywhere: never JSON-parse big lines; filter with line.contains('"type":"..."') first, then serde_json parse only matches. Reuse this in any transcript extractor.

account_usage.rs gives per-session final token totals + model (last token_count + last turn_context) and cost via metrics::cost_for_usage(model, input, cached, output) — ready-made data for per-conversation cost/token chips in a chat header.

Existing Tauri commands relevant to a chat UI: list_discussions, list_prompt_history, claim_session_for_terminal (maps a just-launched terminal to its session file by filename timestamp only), copy_discussion_to_account, delete_discussion (archive/delete all forks), room_enable/disable/status/messages/send.

No module parses tool calls, reasoning, exec/command events, or agent_message text from rollouts — the OpenCode-style tool-call cards require a brand-new parser for those event types (event vocabulary beyond user_message/agent_message/token_count/turn_context is currently unknown to the codebase).
Code comments and UI strings are in French; kombai.rs is irrelevant to chat (embedded code-server iframe manager).

Live updates for an open chat: (a) tail the HEAD rollout file (mtime already used as last_activity) and emit Tauri events, or (b) RoomState.subscribe() broadcast channel could be bridged to window.emit for push instead of the current room_messages polling

Operator-as-chat-participant: RoomState.operator_post / OPERATOR_IDENT ('operator') + messages_for('operator', since) — the room already models a human<->agents chat with cursors; room_send/room_messages are the existing IPC channel

Terminal->session binding: claim_session_for_terminal(accountId, afterUnix, excludeSessionIds, matchSessionId) links a freshly spawned PTY to its rollout uuid by filename timestamp — the key to knowing WHICH JSONL file backs the currently-open chat tab; codex resume <rollout_id> is the documented resume target (DiscussionSummary.rolloutId)

MCP server surface: axum router POST /mcp with Bearer CST_ROOM_TOKEN (unique per PTY, injected by the app); provision_home writes [mcp_servers.agent_room] into each account's config.toml via `codex mcp add`

Per-session metadata for chat headers: DiscussionSummary (title, preview, cwd, messageCount, totalTokens, cliVersion, forkCount) and account_usage scan (model + cumulative tokens + cost via metrics::cost_for_usage)
Room persistence file: <agent_room_data_dir>/messages.jsonl (settings::agent_room_data_dir, honors CST_DATA_DIR); replayable history with monotonic u64 ids as cursors
risks: No transcript parser exists: agent_message payloads, tool calls, exec/command events, and reasoning events in rollout JSONL are never deserialized anywhere — the event schema for tool-call cards must be reverse-engineered from real rollout files (only user_message, agent_message, token_count, turn_context, session_meta are known to the code).

Live chat cannot be fed from the current pipeline: terminals stream raw PTY bytes to xterm.js; rollout JSONL is written by the Codex CLI asynchronously, so a chat view driven by file tailing may lag or interleave oddly mid-turn (partial lines), and there is no file-watcher infrastructure yet (all reads are full on-demand rescans).

Fork/resume complexity: a conversation spans N files sharing payload.session_id; transcripts must read the HEAD file (which re-embeds prior history per the message_count=max assumption in merge_fork_group) — if that assumption ever breaks (fork from an earlier point), transcripts would silently truncate or diverge.

Performance: scan-everything-per-call design (every rollout of every account re-read on each list_discussions/list_prompt_history) is O(total history) — acceptable for dashboards, but a chat UI refreshing per message would need caching/incremental reads; the contains-prefilter pattern must be kept to avoid parsing huge agent lines.

agent_room is a separate message universe from Codex discussions (room chat != session transcript); conflating them in one chat UI risks confusion — room messages are capped at 8000 chars, deduped when consecutive-identical, rate-limited (20 burst / 1 msg/s per agent), and agents/idents reset on app restart (only the message log persists).

Frontend room UI updates by polling room_messages (no push events to the webview); scaling that pattern to per-token chat streaming would require adding Tauri events or bridging the broadcast channel.

Read-only invariants documented in discussions.rs (only delete_discussion moves files; copy never writes to source) should be preserved — a chat UI that writes into rollout files would break Codex CLI's ownership of them.

All user-facing strings and comments are French; new chat UI must match. Titles/previews are char-truncated (80/200) and prompt texts to 600 chars — existing APIs are insufficient for full message rendering, do not reuse them as a transcript source.
